chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one narrator, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام: “Does anything among these hours prevent you from performing salat over funerals?” He said: “No.”

key_terms.السَّاعَاتِ: the times or hours being asked about in relation to prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat, here referring specifically to the funeral prayer
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزِ: funerals, meaning the deceased over whom the prayer is performed
key_terms.لَا: a direct negation indicating no prohibition in this case
key_terms.يَمْنَعُكَ: prevents or restrains you from doing something

ai.seo_question: Can salat over the deceased be performed during normally restricted hours?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no time among the questioned hours that prevents performing salat over the deceased. It indicates the permissibility of funeral prayer without restriction by those times and reflects a jurisprudential ruling concerning rites for the dead.
